newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Profit-takers continue to depress Zimbabwe stocks.
newsitem.headline: Profit-takers continue to depress Zimbabwe stocks.

text.p: Zimbabwean stocks closed weaker on Monday amid continuing profit-taking with brokers saying they expected the market to slide for the next few days before stabilising.
"We are still seeing some profit-taking and the market is sliding. It looks like it will slide for a few more days before stabilising," one broker said.

The key 57-share industrial index dropped 25.84 points to close at 8,099.64, depressed mainly by publishing group Zimpapers's 400-cent fall to 2,100 and cigarette manufacturer Rothmans' 200-cent slide to 3,800.
Also among the losers, sugar producer Hippo shed 20 cents to 930 while packaging firm Hunyani and tyre manufacturer Dunlop lost 10 cents each to 350 and 150 respectively.

Transport group Clan, textiler David Whitehead, local conglomerate TA Holdings, clothing and furniture retailer Tedco and finance group UDC all eased five cents to 335, 75, 160, 745 and 245 respectively.

Against the trend, Alloys rose 50 cents to 850, construction and plastics investor IHL gained 25 cents to 1,825, winery Afdis climbed 15 cents up to 400 and construction firm Mash put on five cents to 225.
In minings, gold producer Ashanti, nickel miner Bindura and Wankie Colliery all traded at previous levels while Falgold lost 15 cents to 110.
The seven-share mining index ended 7.18 points down at 1,207.27.
